BiblicalUsage: A gushing, an issue — the word appears once, in Ezekiel's charge against Oholibah, where the lovers of Egypt are described in coarse, bodily terms. The prophet's language is deliberately ugly, because the idolatry it pictures is ugly. The word is the physical emblem of a spiritual adultery.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Ezekiel's ugly words are honest words: idolatry looks respectable until God shows what it really is.
